_readme: THE RUNG MANIFEST — the single authority on what a rung is.
A rung is an entry in this file. Not a path convention, not a directory, not a naming
convention. Path conventions were tried and failed: a close condition that matched a path
STRING went green with nine rung files still shipping. A string can be satisfied by a tree
that violates the property; a manifest gives you a SET with a declared cardinality, which
is the thing an exact-count assertion can be written against.
TWO FACETS, DELIBERATELY SEPARATE. They answer different questions and must not be conflated:
owns[]   — WHICH FILES DIE when a lower rung is ejected.   (severability / `pnpm eject`)
target   — WHERE THE SHELL SENDS YOU for this rung.        (routing / the shape-routed shell)
A rung's files and a rung's entry point are not the same thing: rungs 1-3 own files in two
language planes but share ONE surface, and rung 4 owns a whole app served from another origin.
OWNERSHIP IS TOTAL AND DISJOINT. Every tracked file is owned by exactly one rung or matched
by `shared`. A file matching neither is a hard CI failure, and `shared` is an enumerated
allowlist rather than a fallback — otherwise 'forgot to classify' becomes the way to pass.
NOT IN SCOPE, ON PURPOSE — do not add these: stream topology, threadId/runId, endpoint URLs,
graph names, or anything describing how a run is carried. `shape` declares the interaction
kind and the shape handler owns everything downstream of that. Rung 4 is the reason: real
Open SWE registers three graphs that do NOT share a run, so any per-rung `threadId` or single
stream endpoint would bake in a topology that is already known to be wrong. See
apps/open-swe/docs/LOCAL-AGENT.md 'Topology: this backend is single-run'.

states.implemented: Present in this repo and runnable from a clean fork.
states.external-required: Present, but needs a service or account this repo cannot provide.
states.planned: Declared in the ladder, not present in the repo. ownedFileCount MUST be 0.

rungs._stateNote: Sourced but not vendored: upstream iliazlobin/software-developer-agent (TypeScript, MIT, frozen). #12 will vendor it. Until then ownedFileCount MUST stay 0 — the planned-rung tripwire fails CI if any file starts claiming this rung without this entry being updated first.

_note: Rung-agnostic paths. An ENUMERATED ALLOWLIST, never a fallback: adding to it is a
deliberate, reviewable edit, so a rung file cannot become 'shared' by being forgotten.
packages/{edge,remix,sveltekit} are here because they are HOST-FRAMEWORK PORTS on an axis
orthogonal to the ladder — each hardcodes no adapter and takes one as a caller option
(edge/src/types.ts, sveltekit/src/handler.ts, remix/src/handler.ts all say so). An ejected
repo at any rung keeps every framework port.
_sharedExceptions: The globs above are evaluated AFTER rung ownership, so a rung-owned file inside a shared
tree (e.g. packages/server/src/adapters/langchain.ts inside packages/server/**) stays owned
by its rung. Rung ownership always wins; `shared` only catches what no rung claimed.
_knownRungNamedNote: C7 flags any shared file whose path segments name a rung, because a broad shared glob can
swallow a rung file silently (docs/rungs/4-open-swe.md under `docs/**` was a real instance).
These entries are the genuine exceptions, and each needs a reason:
package name, not the deepagents rung. The rung's file inside it (ai_backends/deepagents.py)
is claimed by rung 3's `owns` and so never reaches this allowlist.
apps/fastapi-backend/** — its ai_backends/ package is named for the rung axis generally;
the per-rung modules inside are individually rung-owned.
Adding a line here is a deliberate, reviewable act. That is the point: a rung file cannot
become 'shared' by being forgotten, only by someone writing it down.
_rendererNote: DEV7 found nine rung-named renderers in packages/react classified as shared, and was right
that it was wrong. Applying TEAMLEAD's rule -- assign to the LOWEST rung that EMITS the
payload, since higher rungs inherit through `requires` -- per card rather than as a block:
rung 3 (deepagentsEnrich emits): TodoCard data-todo, FileCard data-file,
SubAgentCard data-sub-agent. FileCard and SubAgentCard are emitted by BOTH
enrichers; rung 3 is the lower, and rung 4 inherits them via requires.
rung 4 (openSweEnrich ONLY):     PlanCard data-plan, and PlanProgress, which renders
inside PlanCard and so moves with it.
SHARED, and moving them would have been a BUG: ApprovalCard consumes
data-approval-required and HumanResponseCard data-human-response, both emitted by
approval-gating.ts -- which #30 moved into CORE. Filing them under a rung would
make `eject langgraph` delete the UI for a CORE feature.
useApprovalCardController serves ApprovalCard and follows it.
SHARED, but flagged: TaskCard (data-task) and AgentsMdCard (data-agents-md) have NO
emitter anywhere in this repo -- both parts are declared in react/src/schemas.ts
and exercised only by hand-crafted SSE in tests and e2e. A consumer's own backend
may emit them, so they are not dead code in a library; in a reference
implementation they are a contract with no producer. Raised as issue #50, with both resolutions and no recommendation; PRODUCT rules.

_topologyNote: TOPOLOGIES ARE PER (RUNG, RUNTIME), NEVER PER RUNG. The ladder has exactly one ragged cell:
deep-research exists only in deepagents x fastapi -- verified by reading TOPOLOGIES in all six
ai_backends modules. A rung-level topologies[] array cannot express that: it would either emit
a django x deep-research cell that 404s, or silently drop fastapi's real one.
`topologies: []` means ONE CELL WITH NO TOPOLOGY AXIS -- not zero cells. `run` rungs have no
topology axis, and if empty collapsed to zero they would vanish from the matrix silently.
Rather than leave that to be re-derived by each of the three consumers, rungs.generated.ts
EXPORTS matrixCells(): a semantic that can be guessed wrong should be a function, not a comment.
`runtimes` is NOT `languages`. languages = which language planes hold FILES this rung owns, and
drives the severability eject matrix. runtimes = which backends SERVE this rung, and drives the
behavioural matrix. Rung 1 has languages [ts, py] (it owns a TS adapter AND two Python modules)
but runtimes [django, fastapi] (no node runtime serves it). They are close enough to be
conflated and different enough that conflating them would be wrong.
